subject: Consolidated paperwork for capacity uplift — legal Q&A and sign path
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire@apexcloud.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: dana.ruiz@apexcloud.io
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Capacity and term alignment for upcoming renewal

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on timing. We want to move forward with the 18-month term and the two-step capacity increase (Q1 + Q3). Before we sign, legal at Apex asked for three clarifications:

1) Proration on the first uplift (Q1) — they want credits if the onboarding date slips more than 30 days.
2) A one-sentence carveout on data residency for EU customers (we only have a small EU footprint).
3) Confirmation that Redwood will maintain the current indemnity cap for third-party claims tied to model outputs.

I've attached the OrderForm v2 you shared last week. Can your legal ops review the three asks and confirm whether they can be accommodated in an addendum or need MSA edits?

Claire
Director, Cloud Ops
Apex Cloud

Attachments: RI_OrderForm_Apex_v2.pdf
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Claire Thompson <claire@apexcloud.io>, Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@apexcloud.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Capacity and term alignment for upcoming renewal

Claire, Dana — thanks, noted. Looping in Marissa (customer success) and Ben (AE) so we can coordinate sign path and billing.

Quick answers while legal takes a look:
- Proration: we can offer a credit policy for onboarding delays >30 days but need to define triggers in the Order Form or an Exhibit.
- Data residency carveout: feasible as an Exhibit note — low-friction.
- Indemnity cap: this is legal territory — will confirm whether we can keep the current language or propose a limited carveout.

Marissa — can you confirm the onboarding milestones and the expected Q1 uplift date? Ben — want to confirm the commercial signal we promised (one-time onboarding credit) so we can map billing adjustments.

Olga
Head, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity and term alignment for upcoming renewal

Olga / Ben — tentative milestone below (internal):
- Q1 uplift: target 2027-01-15 (customer readiness check 2026-12-15)
- Q3 uplift: target 2027-07-01

If onboarding slips >30 days from the target, we can offer a pro-rated credit equal to the monthly token commitment for the delayed period (max 3 months). That keeps the math simple and mirrors past playbooks.

Kimberly — legal asked to propose where this sits (Order Form credit clause vs Exhibit). From an ops perspective, Exhibit is easier to version.

Marissa
Customer Success

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Capacity and term alignment for upcoming renewal — legal redlines attached

Team — attaching a redline of the MSA and a proposed exhibit for credits and data residency. High-level notes:

- Proration / credit: added Exhibit C, Section 2.1 (onboarding credit). Language defines triggers (missed onboarding milestone >30 days), credit calculation (monthly committed units prorated), and a cure period. This avoids changing core billing language in the Order Form.
- Data residency: short Exhibit note to reflect limited EU jurisdiction for subset of workloads; does not change host locations for primary environment.
- Indemnity cap: we cannot expand exposure. Proposed compromise: preserve current cap but add a narrowly scoped exception for breaches of Redwood's security obligations (we will not accept broader model-output indemnities).

I've also attached a consolidated Order Form (RI_OrderForm_Apex_v2) with the Exhibit references.

Please review and flag commercial or CS objections — want to send to Apex legal tomorrow morning.

Attachments: redlines_MSA_v3.docx; exhibit-C-capacity-matrix.xlsx
From: Claire Thompson <claire@apexcloud.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@apexcloud.io>, legal@apexcloud.io
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Consolidated paperwork for capacity uplift — legal Q&A and sign path

Olga / Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the redlines. Our legal reviewed and provided two modest edits (inline):

1) On Exhibit C credit cure period: they want the cure window to be 45 days instead of 30; they have an internal deployment approval process that can add delay.
2) Indemnity language: Apex can accept the limited security-breach carveout but asked for a reciprocal statement confirming Redwood's right to pause service in the event of customer misuse (we already discussed pausing for abuse).

Commercially, we also want to confirm the sign path: Apex legal will sign the MSA amend + Exhibit, and Claire will countersign the Order Form after DocuSign arrives. Can you send the consolidated DocuSign (exhibits + order form) once you incorporate the two edits?

If we close by Oct 20, we can still hit the Jan uplift date.

Best,
Claire
Director, Cloud Ops, Apex Cloud
